items.title: Ruth Brown interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995
items.q: I did 'Why Do You Whisper Green Grass' which was an old Bill Kenny tune from the Inkspots, you know which dates back to my youth.

ctx.x: Tell us one of the ones that’s pretty good. Tell us one of the ones that you think is classic.
I did an album in 1965 called “Ruth Brown ‘65” on Mainstream. The company went out of business. The record has been re-issued this year on SONY under a new name, it’s © Fillius Jazz Archive -13-

now called “Softly.” And in that album I did “Here’s That Rainy Day,” I did “Why Do You Whisper Green Grass” which was an old Bill Kenny tune from the Inkspots, you know which dates back to my youth. And in that I also did “Porgy” — “I Love You Porgy.” Things that I had forgotten that I’d ever touched on. And I was listening to that album and I said, [whistles] I didn’t sound bad, you know?
